as_told.title: 1943 reverse engineering of a German pulse jet

plain: Wright Field was a US military airfield where aircraft were tested and developed. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in 1943 engineers there successfully reverse engineered a German pulse jet, a simple jet engine that fires in rapid bursts, meaning they took apart a captured engine and worked out how to build it. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells the same story in nearly the same words. They raise it to show that the US already had a track record of copying technology it did not invent, which would matter if it ever got hold of something stranger.
